title: Security seams: queue authority is not object-method permission
summary: VMM uses distinct authority mechanisms at distinct seams. Queue Fabric ACL/message admission protects cross-company and venue boundaries; exact object×method permission belongs only where a VMM object method is actually exposed through Security Manager.
invariants: Do not decorate queue-only message boundaries with Access Permissions merely because the module exists.
Federation principals have no ACL on VMM direct-institutional default/close-out product queues.
The browser never receives VMM engine/service/Queue Fabric authority objects.
When a protected VMM method is exposed through Security Manager, evaluate exact object×method permission there.

provenance.claim: One-book boundary plus explicit rule that Access Permissions is not decoratively applied to Queue Fabric message boundaries.
Browser/service authority separation and exact action-layer rule.
